summary: This file exports helper functions and constants for rendering a blog article graph visualization. It handles filtering which nodes and edges to display, calculating how to fit the graph onto a canvas, sizing text labels, and grouping articles by category. All the layout math is kept separate from UI code so it's easier to understand and modify.

explanations.79: The function accepts an optional object with mainTag and topN properties; if neither is passed, it uses empty defaults (the `= {}` at the end).
explanations.84: We spread `nodes` into a new array before sorting because sorting mutates the original array — this way we don't accidentally change the input data.
explanations.90: This takes a Set instead of an array for fast lookup: checking if a permalink exists in a Set is much quicker than searching through a list.
explanations.108: If there are no visible nodes, we return a neutral transform (no scaling, no movement) to avoid crashes from trying to calculate a bounding box on empty data.
explanations.118: We subtract and add the node's radius to find the edges of its circular boundary, not just its center point.
explanations.124: The `Math.max(..., 1)` prevents division by zero later — if all nodes are at the same spot, we treat the span as 1 unit instead of 0.
explanations.128: We take the minimum of two ratios to ensure the graph fits in both directions, then cap it at 4 so we never zoom in more than 4x.
explanations.143: This returns null when there's fewer than 2 nodes because you need at least two points to define a meaningful width-to-height ratio.
explanations.203: The `??` operator means 'use maxRatio if contentAspectRatio returned null' — a fallback when we don't have enough nodes to measure shape.
explanations.206: We calculate density as a fraction (0 to 1) of how many visible nodes there are compared to the default view; fewer nodes get a smaller canvas.
explanations.208: We use `Math.sqrt(density)` so the height shrinks gently with fewer nodes rather than dropping sharply — avoids jarring size jumps.
explanations.245: The `!` tells TypeScript we know `degree.get(edge.source)` won't be undefined here because we initialized all node permalinks on line 243.
explanations.264: If a node's permalink isn't in the degree map (shouldn't happen), we treat it as degree 0 — safer than crashing.
explanations.276: Orphan nodes get a minimum size floor so they're still visible and clickable; connected nodes keep their data-driven size.
